<output>
# Dust

A small command-line tool to quickly see which directories and files are using the most disk space.

Demo:

![Example](media/snap.png)

Overview

Dust prints a compact view of the biggest subdirectories or files. It automatically recurses into large subtrees so you can quickly find the biggest consumers of disk space. The display uses bars and colors to indicate relative usage and which parent folders subfolders belong to.

Usage

```
Usage: dust
Usage: dust <dir>
Usage: dust <dir> <another_dir> <and_more>
Usage: dust -p  (full-path - Show fullpath of the subdirectories)
Usage: dust -s  (apparent-size - shows the length of the file as opposed to the amount of disk space it uses)
Usage: dust -n 30  (Shows 30 directories instead of the default [default is terminal height])
Usage: dust -d 3  (Shows 3 levels of subdirectories)
Usage: dust -D (Show only directories)
Usage: dust -F (Show only files - finds your largest files)
Usage: dust -r (reverse order of output)
Usage: dust -o si/b/kb/kib/mb/mib/gb/gib (output format)
Usage: dust -X ignore  (ignore all files and directories with the name 'ignore')
Usage: dust -x (Only show directories on the same filesystem)
Usage: dust -b (Do not show percentages or draw ASCII bars)
Usage: dust -B (--bars-on-right - Percent bars moved to right side of screen)
Usage: dust -i (Do not show hidden files)
Usage: dust -c (No colors [monochrome])
Usage: dust -C (Force colors)
Usage: dust -f (Count files instead of diskspace)
Usage: dust -t (Group by filetype)
Usage: dust -z 10M (min-size, Only include files larger than 10M)
Usage: dust -e regex (Only include files matching this regex)
Usage: dust -v regex (Exclude files matching this regex)
Usage: dust -L (dereference-links - Treat symlinks as directories)
Usage: dust -P (Disable the progress indicator)
Usage: dust -R (For screen readers. Removes bars/symbols. Adds new column: depth level.)
Usage: dust -S (Custom Stack size)
Usage: dust --skip-total (No total row will be displayed)
Usage: dust -j (Prints JSON representation of directories)
Usage: dust --files0-from=FILE (Read NUL-terminated file paths from FILE)
Usage: dust --files-from=FILE (Read newline-terminated file paths from FILE)
Usage: dust --collapse=node-modules (Keep node_modules collapsed in display)
```

Config

Dust can read configuration from `~/.config/dust/config.toml` or `~/.dust.toml` to set default options.

Alternatives

- NCDU
- dutree
- dua
- pdu
- dirstat-rs

</output>

    /// assert!(arg_value.matches("FAST", true));
    /// assert!(!arg_value.matches("FAST", false));
    /// ```
    pub fn matches(&self, value: &str, ignore_case: bool) -> bool {
        if ignore_case {
            self.get_name_and_aliases()
                .any(|name| eq_ignore_case(name, value))
        } else {
            self.get_name_and_aliases().any(|name| name == value)
        }
    }

/// Walks a directory tree, returning the root node.
pub fn walk(
    path: &Path,
    filters: &Filters,
    measure: &Measure,
    errors: &mut WalkErrors,
) -> Option<Node> {
    // metadata for the root
    let md = if filters.dereference_links {
        std::fs::metadata(path)
    } else {
        std::fs::symlink_metadata(path)
    };
    let md = match md {
        Ok(m) => m,
        Err(e) => {
            errors.add(path, &e);
            return None;
        }
    };
    // does it look like a directory we can list?
    match std::fs::read_dir(path) {
        Ok(entries) => {
            let kind = resolve_kind(path, &md);
            let own = file_size(&md, measure);
            let own_time = file_time(&md, TimeField::Mtime);
            let mut node = Node::new(display_name(path), path.to_path_buf(), 0, kind, is_executable(&md));
            node.own_size = match measure {
                Measure::FileCount => 0,
                Measure::FileTime(_) => own_time,
                _ => own,
            };
            let own_time = file_time(&md, TimeField::Mtime);
            let mut total = own;
            let mut max_time = own_time;
            let mut count = 0u64;
            for entry in entries.filter_map(|e| e.ok()) {
                let child_path = entry.path();
                if skip_entry(&child_path, &entry, filters, measure) {
                    continue;
                }
                let child = walk_child(&child_path, filters, measure, errors);
                if let Some(c) = child {
                    match measure {
                        Measure::FileCount | Measure::Blocks | Measure::Apparent => {
                            total += c.size;
                            count += c.size;
                        }
                        Measure::FileTime(_) => {
                            if c.size > max_time {
                                max_time = c.size;
                            }
                        }
                    }
                    node.children.push(c);
                }

  if [ "$a" == "$b" ]; then pass=$((pass+1)); else fail=$((fail+1)); failed+=("$desc"); fi
}

  run -c -R -r $d
  run -c -p $d

run -c -p t c3

/// Formats a size according to the output format.
pub fn format_data(value: u64, of: OutputFormat) -> String {
    match of {
        OutputFormat::Auto => {
            let value = value as f64;
            if value < 1024f64 {
                format!("{}B", value as u64)
            } else {
                let (div, suffix) = binary_unit(value);
                let v = value / div;
                if v < 10f64 {
                    format!("{:.1}{}", v, suffix)
                } else {
                    format!("{:.0}{}", v, suffix)
                }
            }
        }
        OutputFormat::Si => {
            let value = value as f64;
            if value < 1000f64 {
                format!("{}B", value as u64)
            } else {
                let (div, suffix) = si_unit(value);
                let v = value / div;
                if v < 10f64 {
                    format!("{:.1}{}", v, suffix)
                } else {
                    format!("{}{}", v as u64, suffix)
                }
</output>

# dust 1.2.3 re-implementation — status report

## What this is
An original Rust re-implementation of `dust` (Like du but more intuitive), version 1.2.3,
built from behavioural observation of the provided `./executable` (no source was consulted).

## Build
`./compile.sh` runs `cargo build --release --offline` and copies `target/release/dust`
to `./executable`.  Dependencies (clap 4.6.1, regex, serde_json, toml) are resolved from the
pre-populated cargo registry cache, so no network is needed.

Verified: `./executable -V` â `Dust 1.2.3`, help/usage/errors match the original byte for byte
including the `[possible values: ...]` blocks, the `-o` ignore-case behaviour and the
`--only-dir` vs `--only-file`/`--file-types` conflict errors.

## Already matching (verified with a diff harness over many flag/dir combinations)
* CLI parsing, `--help`, `-h`, `--version`, value-parsing errors, conflicts.
* Tree layout: size column width, `┌─┴`/`├─┬` branch glyphs, indentation, per-depth name field.
* Bar drawing (`█▒░`+space segments, ancestor shading by real depth, fill =
  `size*(bar_width-1)/total + 1`, capped), percent rounding (banker's rounding via `{:.0}`).
* `-r` (pre-order descending, mirrored glyphs), `-B` (bar right-aligned, trailing space),
  `-R` screen-reader mode, `-b`, `-p`, `-j` JSON, `-o` formats (auto/si/b/k/m/g/t/kb/mb/gb/tb),
  `-s`, `-f` (only regular files count), `-i`, `-D`, `-F` (flattened leaves at depth 1),
  `-t` (type groups), `-d` (prunes first, then `-n`; with `-d` and no `-n` the limit is
  disabled), `-n` (global top-N over the depth-pruned tree, tie-break by (size,name)),
  `--skip-total` (children become the top level, real depth kept for bar_left),
  `--collapse`, `-X` (exact name match), `-v`/`-e`/`-I` regex filters, `-z` (leading digits +
  K/M/G/T/P suffix, 1024 base unless the suffix contains `B`, warning text included),
  `-L`, `-x`, config file handling (`--config`, `~/.dust.toml`, `~/.config/dust/config.toml`,
  precedence and all the "Ignoring invalid config file ..." messages).
* Panic messages reproduced at the original source positions:
  `-M`/`-A`/`-y` bad value â `src/config.rs:203:41` "invalid data format";
  `-I` unreadable â `src/main.rs:184:14` unwrap message;
  small `-w` â `src/display.rs:142:5` / `src/display.rs:308:5`.
* Colours when stdout is a TTY (size red for the biggest child / root, dir `1;34`,
  executable `1;32`, fifo `33`, socket `1;35`).

## Known remaining differences (todo)
1. `--skip-total` bar *segments*: the ancestor shading/fill in that mode differs
   (upstream appears to derive boundaries from display depth / a different ancestor chain).
   Only the bar interior is affected, the columns/percent are correct.
2. `-F`/`-t` interact with `--skip-total` for a few trees (same root cause as (1)).
3. `-j` for paths with invalid UTF-8: upstream panics at `src/main.rs:328:53`
   (`path contains invalid UTF-8 characters`); we currently emit lossy names.
4. Progress output on stderr (`Indexing: ... `-` spinner`, `Preparing: ...`) is
   implemented with the same format/thresholds but its exact interleaving is timing
   dependent in the original, so it is only approximately reproduced.
5. Error list ordering for `No such file or directory: a, b` is hash-ordered in the
   original (non-deterministic); we use a HashSet as well but the order can differ.
6. `-t` combined with `-f`, `-L`, `-i` edge cases and `-M`/`-A`/`-y` day-boundary
   semantics were only partially cross-checked (date-based difference, `n+1` shift).
7. `~/..dust.toml` vs `~/.config/dust/config.toml` precedence when the first fails to parse
   needs a second look (currently falls back, matching observed behaviour in the tested cases).
EOF
